newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen trapped in narrow range in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen trapped in narrow range in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is likely to move in a narrow range versus the yen in Asia on Thursday, as the market's attention is expected to shift from dollar/yen to European currencies, particularly sterling.
Worries about Japan's growing trade surplus persist, but the market lacks fresh incentives to push the greenback lower in the near term, traders said.
"Dollar/yen is likely to move narrowly today. After downside probes failed yesterday, people are becoming wary of pushing the dollar sharply below 112.50 yen," said a trader at a trust bank.

The Japan-U.S. Business Council meeting in San Francisco ended on Wednesday with U.S. and Japanese business leaders calling for steps to minimise a rise in the Japanese trade surplus and to stabilise the yen-dollar exchange rate within "an appropriate range".
"The market seems to have ran out of incentives for dollar/yen for now with the end of the Business Council meeting," said the trust bank trader.
If Japanese stocks and government bonds show big price swings, however, that could have some impact on dollar/yen, traders said.
On Wednesday, the Nikkei 225 stock average's slide was partly responsible for discouraging yen buying, traders said.
Operators are waiting for Bank of England's decision on interest rates at its monetary policy meeting which ends later on Thursday.
Most market participants expect the BOE to raise interest rates by a quarter point.
"The market seems to have already factored in an interest rate hike of 25 basis points. If the BOE decides to raise rates by 50 basis points, sterling could rally," said a city bank trader.

Early in New York trade on Wednesday, the dollar rose to 1.7655 marks, its highest level since February 1994, mostly as a result of continued mark selling by investors concerned that Europe will replace the German currency with a broad-based, but weak single currency in 1999.
The greenback, however, retreated below 1.7600 marks following a late slide in the Dow Jones industrial average, which closed down almost 120 points.
The dollar ended at 112.71/81 yen and 1.7598/08 marks on Wednesday in New York.
